questions.q: In the equilibrium, $A B \rightleftharpoons A+B$, if the equilibrium concentration of $A$ is double, then equilibrium concentration of $B$ will be
questions.solution:
For the equilibrium reaction $AB \rightleftharpoons A + B$, the equilibrium constant $K_{eq}$ is given by the expression:

$K_{eq} = \dfrac{[A][B]}{[AB]}$

Since $K_{eq}$ is a constant at a fixed temperature, the product of the concentrations of the products divided by the concentration of the reactant remains constant. Let the initial equilibrium concentrations be $[A]_1$, $[B]_1$, and $[AB]_1$. Then $K_{eq} = \dfrac{[A]_1 [B]_1}{[AB]_1}$.

If the equilibrium concentration of $A$ is doubled, let the new concentration be $[A]_2 = 2[A]_1$. Assuming the concentration of the reactant $[AB]$ remains effectively constant or the system adjusts such that the ratio is maintained, we have:

$\dfrac{[A]_1 [B]_1}{[AB]} = \dfrac{[A]_2 [B]_2}{[AB]}$

$[A]_1 [B]_1 = (2[A]_1) [B]_2$

$[B]_2 = \dfrac{[A]_1 [B]_1}{2[A]_1} = \dfrac{1}{2} [B]_1$

Therefore, the equilibrium concentration of $B$ becomes half of its original value.

Answer: half

The chemical equation for the reaction is $3 \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{6}(\mathrm{g})$.

$[\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}]^{3} = \dfrac{0.5}{4} = 0.125$

$[\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}] = (0.125)^{1/3} = (0.5^{3})^{1/3} = 0.5 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$.

Answer: $0.5 \mathrm{~mol} / \mathrm{L}$

questions.q: For the reaction $2 \mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5 \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2$. If inital pressure is $100 \mathrm{~atm}$ and rate constant $k$ is $3.38 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. After $20 \mathrm{~min}$ the final pressure of $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ will be
questions.solution:
The reaction $2 \mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5 \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{NO}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2$ is a first-order reaction. The rate equation for a first-order reaction is given by $P_t = P_0 e^{-kt}$, where $P_0$ is the initial pressure and $P_t$ is the pressure at time $t$.

Given values are:
$P_0 = 100 \text{ atm}$
$k = 3.38 \times 10^{-5} \text{ s}^{-1}$
$t = 20 \text{ min} = 20 \times 60 \text{ s} = 1200 \text{ s}$

Substituting these values into the equation:
$P_t = 100 \times e^{-(3.38 \times 10^{-5}) \times 1200}$

Calculate the exponent:
$-(3.38 \times 10^{-5}) \times 1200 = -0.04056$

Now calculate $P_t$:
